## Summary - Implement the engine-level fault-tolerance framework proposed in #22344 for coordinated fault handling across a distributed SGLang deployment. - Expose status and control APIs that let upper-layer serving frameworks control the fault-handling process. - Integrate with Mooncake Elastic EP to support fault-driven scale-down and continued serving on surviving ranks. ## Motivation Mooncake Elastic EP already provides **runtime-level elasticity** for MoE inference, including failed-rank isolation, expert redistribution, continued execution on surviving ranks, and replacement-rank recovery. This PR builds on the Elastic EP work #8961 , with runtime scaling discussed in #22788 . The recovery action appropriate for a service depends on more than a runtime failure signal. A communication timeout caused by transient network disruption may call for waiting and retrying, while a persistent failure may require removing workers. Maintenance policy may also require taking an entire node out of service when only one device fails. Choosing among these actions requires information from monitoring and orchestration outside the inference runtime. The [Dynamo DP-aware health check](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/7466) illustrates why serving frameworks need visibility into the health of individual DP ranks within an engine. [vLLM’s fault-tolerance framework](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44428) also implements fault reporting and an interface for externally directed recovery in DP+EP deployments. This motivates a consistent **engine-level interface** through which the serving framework can observe fault state and coordinate its chosen response. The engine must turn that response into consistent worker actions and request-routing decisions. Keeping this control path separate from backend execution also provides a common integration boundary for devices whose recovery procedures differ. We therefore separate fault handling into three responsibilities: the runtime performs backend-specific isolation and recovery; SGLang aggregates engine state and executes control instructions; the serving framework chooses and orchestrates the recovery policy. The FT framework adds this control path alongside the existing serving architecture, using Mooncake Elastic EP as the initial data-plane integration. ## Architecture Overview The FT Manager collects scheduler and process reports and coordinates instructions from the serving framework. The FT Manager is drawn separately for clarity; it is hosted in TokenizerManager. Yellow marks the new component; dashed lines mark FT reporting and control. ![Fault-tolerance architecture](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/gaidandawang-afk/5a7b5d2f0ad1e4c7672c5c81af9339aa/raw/88a116d62e361278f1d070a44ecab1c965585ed6/architecture-overview.svg) The API labels refer to HTTP-server endpoints. The reporting line groups scheduler reports and independently sent watchdog reports. | API | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `GET /v1/fault_tolerance/status` | Query cluster fault state and the result of a control request. | | `POST /v1/fault_tolerance/apply` | Submit the recovery action selected by the serving framework. | The serving framework chooses between two actions: - **`retry`:** retry execution while retaining the current serving topology. - **`scale_down`:** remove the selected DP replicas and resume serving with the remaining capacity. Accepted actions return HTTP 202. The caller polls status for the matching request ID to confirm completion. ## Modifications ### 1. Add per-node fault-tolerance watchdogs Add a dedicated watchdog on each node to monitor local scheduler processes, report process exits and periodic heartbeats, and execute targeted DP shutdown requests. The FT Manager aggregates these reports and marks the node's scheduler processes unavailable when its heartbeat expires. ```text Node 0 watchdog -- process reports / heartbeat --+ Node 1 watchdog -- process reports / heartbeat --+--> FT Manager Node N watchdog -- process reports / heartbeat --+ ``` Unlike the fail-fast subprocess watchdog, the FT watchdog reports individual scheduler-process exits while continuing to monitor the remaining processes. Its control endpoint and heartbeat loop remain active even after all local scheduler processes have exited. ### 2. Add the FT Manager The FT Manager provides a cluster-wide view of faults and coordinates the response selected by the serving framework. - Combine scheduler exceptions, process liveness, and runtime membership to identify affected DP replicas and determine whether new requests can be admitted. - Coordinate `retry` and `scale_down` across the relevant schedulers, tracking acknowledgments and preventing overlapping control operations. - Update admission and routing as the operation completes, and expose its result through the status API. ### 3. Guard scheduler execution Add an exception boundary around the scheduler event loop and command handling for recovery. The state-transition diagram shows the `pause` strategy: ```mermaid flowchart LR Run["Event loop
try / catch"] Pause["Paused
Abort affected requests
Report exception
Wait for instruction"] Command["retry / scale_down
Release KV cache
Restore / update active mask
Run EPLB when required"] Resume[Resume event loop] Run -->|Exception| Pause Pause -->|FT command| Command Command -->|Acknowledge| Resume ``` Schedulers pause locally while continuing to receive control commands. They execute the selected action, clean up the failed request state, and acknowledge completion before resuming inference. The exception boundary and command handling are independent of the communication backend; backend-specific actions are invoked during command execution. ### Scale-down Sequence The following sequence illustrates fault-driven scale-down with the `pause` strategy. Process-exit reports and scheduler-exception reports arrive independently; either causes the FT Manager to block new request admission. The serving framework selects the DP replicas to remove, and the engine coordinates shutdown, expert redistribution, and routing updates before reopening admission. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant F as Serving Framework participant M as FT Manager participant W as Node Watchdog participant D as DP Controller participant S as Surviving Schedulers Note over W,S: A scheduler process fails par Process monitoring W->>M: Report process exit and Runtime fault detection S->>S: Detect fault and abort locally tracked in-flight requests S->>S: Pause execution S->>M: Report scheduler exception end Note over M: Admission blocked on the first fault report F->>M: GET /v1/fault_tolerance/status M-->>F: Per-DP fault status F->>M: POST /v1/fault_tolerance/apply (scale_down) M-->>F: 202 Accepted + request_id opt Selected DPs still have live processes M->>W: Stop processes belonging to selected DPs W-->>M: Report process exits end M->>D: Send scale_down with updated active-rank mask D->>S: Forward command to surviving target DPs S->>S: Update mask and run fault-triggered EPLB Note over S: Synchronize surviving ranks after EPLB S->>S: Release failed-request state and clear pause S-->>M: Acknowledge command completion Note over M: New request admission remains blocked M->>D: Update active DP routing D-->>M: Acknowledge routing update Note over M: Record completion and reopen admission F->>M: GET /v1/fault_tolerance/status M-->>F: Matching last_ft_request_id, no ft_error ``` This diagram shows the successful recovery path. Timeout and failure behavior is described below. ## How to Use ### Launch Enable the framework on a Mooncake Elastic EP deployment with DP attention: ```bash python3 -u -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --tp-size 4 \ --dp-size 4 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast \ --enable-dp-lm-head \ --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \ --moe-a2a-backend mooncake \ --elastic-ep-backend mooncake \ --enable-eplb \ --ep-num-redundant-experts 64 \ --deepep-mode low_latency \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \ --attention-backend triton \ --sampling-backend pytorch \ --disable-custom-all-reduce \ --cuda-graph-backend-decode full \ --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \ --enable-fault-tolerance \ --fault-tolerance-on-error-strategy pause \ --fault-tolerance-timeout 30 \ --fault-tolerance-pause-timeout 120 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` - `--enable-fault-tolerance`: enable the fault-tolerance framework. - `--fault-tolerance-pause-timeout`: maximum time, in seconds, a scheduler waits for a recovery command after pausing on an exception. If the deadline expires, the scheduler signals its node's main process to terminate the local process tree. - `--fault-tolerance-timeout`: timeout, in seconds, for each control phase: targeted process shutdown, scheduler-command acknowledgments, and routing-update acknowledgment. This is a per-phase timeout, not a deadline for the entire recovery operation. Control-phase timeouts and unexpected exceptions in the FT Manager's asynchronous tasks trigger fail-stop termination of the process tree containing the FT Manager. In these cases, the status endpoint may become unavailable instead of returning `ft_error`. The serving framework should handle both reported operation errors and loss of endpoint availability. For a killed rank, the two strategies behave as follows: | Strategy | Fault handling | Scale-down | | --- | --- | --- | | `continue` | Mooncake detects the lost rank and continues runtime recovery. | Automatically exclude unavailable ranks from execution and routing based on observed state. | | `pause` | Raise the fault to the scheduler, pause execution, and block new admission. | The serving framework submits `scale_down` to remove the affected DP and resume serving. | `pause` is the default. Use `continue` to retain automatic runtime handling. ### Fault-tolerant Serving 1. Start normal serving with four ranks (`TP/DP/EP = 4`) and the `pause` strategy. Check that all four DP engines are `healthy` and inference succeeds. Keep inference running on a surviving rank while injecting the failure. 2. Kill the scheduler process for rank 3: ```bash kill -9 ``` 3. Query fault status. DP 3 should be `dead`; surviving schedulers that report an exception appear as `unhealthy`. New inference admission is paused. ```bash curl http://localhost:30000/v1/fault_tolerance/status ``` Example response after the surviving schedulers have reported the fault: ```json { "schema_version": 1, "total_engines": 4, "engines": [ {"id": 0, "status": "unhealthy"}, {"id": 1, "status": "unhealthy"}, {"id": 2, "status": "unhealthy"}, {"id": 3, "status": "dead"} ] } ``` 4. Ask the engine to remove DP 3, then query status again: ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:30000/v1/fault_tolerance/apply \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"instruction":"scale_down","params":{"removed_dp_ranks":[3]},"request_id":"scale-down-1"}' curl http://localhost:30000/v1/fault_tolerance/status ``` After completion, status includes the matching `last_ft_request_id` without `ft_error`. DPs 0–2 are `healthy` and DP 3 remains `dead`: ```json { "schema_version": 1, "total_engines": 4, "engines": [ {"id": 0, "status": "healthy"}, {"id": 1, "status": "healthy"}, {"id": 2, "status": "healthy"}, {"id": 3, "status": "dead"} ], "last_ft_request_id": "scale-down-1" } ``` 5. Send inference requests again and confirm that the remaining three ranks serve normally. ## Test Plan The results below were obtained with the combined FT integration on DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat and the paired Mooncake adaptation, using 256 GSM8K questions, 5-shot completion, and temperature 0. | Scenario | Main checks | GSM8K accuracy | | --- | --- | --- | | Kill one rank: 4 → 3, `pause` | External scale-down, completion polling, survivor generation/logprobs, removed-DP routing rejection | 68.36% | | Kill one rank: 4 → 3, `continue` | Automatic shrink, survivor generation/logprobs and routing | 68.36% | | Repeated failures: 4 → 3 → 2, `pause` | Successive control operations, generation/logprobs after each shrink, final accuracy | 68.36% | | Recoverable execution error → `retry` | External retry command, unchanged topology, resumed generation | 68.36% | ## Limitations - The current target platforms are GPU and NPU; MLX and other platforms are outside the scope of this PR. - Both Mooncake backends must be enabled: `--elastic-ep-backend mooncake` for process-group communication and `--moe-a2a-backend mooncake` for MoE dispatch/combine. Other backend combinations are not supported. - The deployment scope is DP attention. Prefill/decode disaggregation support and compatibility with runtime scale-up are follow-up work. - The Mooncake backends currently depend on RDMA. Single-host use depends on an additional Mooncake adaptation, currently in progress, for local communication setup and deferred connection handling on the no-HCA path. The dependency link will be added when submitted. - Requests affected by the fault are discarded. Resuming interrupted requests is follow-up work. ## Cross-References - RFC #22344 - PR #8961 - #30164 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #39185425089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39185425089) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #39185425001](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39185425001) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #39185425039](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39185425039)

DPs 0–2 are `healthy` and DP 3 remains `dead`: ```json { "schema_version": 1, "total_engines": 4, "engines": [ {"id": 0, "status": "healthy"}, {"id": 1, "status": "healthy"}, {"id": 2, "status": "healthy"}, {"id": 3, "status": "dead"} ], "last_ft_request_id": "scale-down-1" } ``` 5. Send inference requests again and confirm that the remaining three ranks serve normally. ## Test Plan The results below were obtained with the combined FT integration on DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat and the paired Mooncake adaptation, using 256 GSM8K questions, 5-shot completion, and temperature 0. | Scenario | Main checks | GSM8K accuracy | | --- | --- | --- | | Kill one rank: 4 → 3, `pause` | External scale-down, completion polling, survivor generation/logprobs, removed-DP routing rejection | 68.36% | | Kill one rank: 4 → 3, `continue` | Automatic shrink, survivor generation/logprobs and routing | 68.36% | | Repeated failures: 4 → 3 → 2, `pause` | Successive control operations, generation/logprobs after each shrink, final accuracy | 68.36% | | Recoverable execution error → `retry` | External retry command, unchanged topology, resumed generation | 68.36% | ## Limitations - The current target platforms are GPU and NPU; MLX and other platforms are outside the scope of this PR. - Both Mooncake backends must be enabled: `--elastic-ep-backend mooncake` for process-group communication and `--moe-a2a-backend mooncake` for MoE dispatch/combine. Other backend combinations are not supported. - The deployment scope is DP attention. Prefill/decode disaggregation support and compatibility with runtime scale-up are follow-up work. - The Mooncake backends currently depend on RDMA. Single-host use depends on an additional Mooncake adaptation, currently in progress, for local communication setup and deferred connection handling on the no-HCA path. The dependency link will be added when submitted. - Requests affected by the fault are discarded. Resuming interrupted requests is follow-up work. ## Cross-References - RFC #22344 - PR #8961 - #30164 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #39185425089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39185425089) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #39185425001](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39185425001) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #39185425039](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39185425039)

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import threading
+from multiprocessing import Process
+
+import zmq
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import (
+    FaultToleranceDPCShutdownReqInput,
+    ProcessActiveRanksOutput,
+    WatchdogHeartbeatOutput,
+    sock_recv,
+    sock_send,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils.network import (
+    NetworkAddress,
+    get_local_ip_auto,
+    get_zmq_socket_on_host,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+FT_WATCHDOG_POLL_INTERVAL = 3.0
+FT_WATCHDOG_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000
+
+
+class DPCFaultToleranceWatchdog:
+    """Own DPC fault-tolerance control sockets in the watchdog thread.
+
+    Unlike SubprocessWatchdog, report individual exits without terminating the
+    service, and keep the node control endpoint alive after its ranks exit.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        context: zmq.Context,
+        tokenizer_endpoint: str,
+        node_rank: int,
+        processes: list[Process],
+        process_dp_ranks: list[int],
+        process_global_ranks: list[int],
+    ) -> None:
+        self._context = context
+        self._tokenizer_endpoint = tokenizer_endpoint
+        self._node_rank = node_rank
+        self._process_dp_ranks = process_dp_ranks
+        self._process_global_ranks = process_global_ranks
+        self._shutdown_receiver = None
+        self._heartbeat_sender = None
+        self._ready = threading.Event()
+        self._start_error: Exception | None = None
+        self.control_endpoint: str | None = None
+        self._processes = processes
+        self._reported: set[int] = set()
+        self._stop_event = threading.Event()
+        self._thread: threading.Thread | None = None
+
+    def start(self) -> None:
+        if self._thread is None:
+            self._thread = threading.Thread(
+                target=self._monitor_loop, daemon=True, name="ft-dpc-watchdog"
+            )
+            self._thread.start()
+        self._ready.wait()
+        if self._start_error is not None:
+            raise self._start_error
+
+    def stop(self) -> None:
+        if self._thread is not None:
+            self._stop_event.set()
+            self._thread.join(timeout=FT_WATCHDOG_POLL_INTERVAL * 2)
+            if not self._thread.is_alive():
+                self._thread = None
+
+    def _monitor_loop(self) -> None:
+        try:
+            self._on_thread_start()
+            # Keep serving control and heartbeats after every local rank exits.
+            while not self._stop_event.wait(FT_WATCHDOG_POLL_INTERVAL):
+                self._check_processes()
+                self._poll_control()
+        except Exception as error:
+            logger.error("DPC FT watchdog thread crashed: %s", error, exc_info=True)
+        finally:
+            self._close_sockets()
+
+    def _check_processes(self) -> None:
+        for index, proc in enumerate(self._processes):
+            if index in self._reported or proc.is_alive() or proc.exitcode is None:
+                continue
+            self._reported.add(index)
+            self._report_process_exit(index, proc)
+
+    def _on_thread_start(self) -> None:
+        try:
+            host = get_local_ip_auto(fallback="127.0.0.1")
+            port, self._shutdown_receiver = get_zmq_socket_on_host(
+                self._context, zmq.PULL, host=host
+            )
+            self.control_endpoint = NetworkAddress(host, port).to_tcp()
+
+            self._heartbeat_sender = self._context.socket(zmq.PUSH)
+            self._heartbeat_sender.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
+            self._heartbeat_sender.setsockopt(zmq.SNDHWM, 1)
+            self._heartbeat_sender.setsockopt(zmq.IMMEDIATE, 1)
+            self._heartbeat_sender.setsockopt(zmq.SNDTIMEO, FT_WATCHDOG_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS)
+            if "[" in self._tokenizer_endpoint:
+                self._heartbeat_sender.setsockopt(zmq.IPV6, 1)
+            self._heartbeat_sender.connect(self._tokenizer_endpoint)
+        except Exception as error:
+            self._start_error = error
+            raise
+        finally:
+            self._ready.set()
+
+    def heartbeat(self) -> WatchdogHeartbeatOutput:
+        return WatchdogHeartbeatOutput(
+            node_rank=self._node_rank,
+            ranks=sorted(self._process_global_ranks),
+            control_endpoint=self.control_endpoint,
+        )
+
+    def _report_process_exit(self, index: int, proc: Process) -> None:
+        dp_rank = self._process_dp_ranks[index]
+        global_rank = self._process_global_ranks[index]
+        logger.warning(
+            "Scheduler global rank %s for DP rank %s exited (pid=%s)",
+            global_rank,
+            dp_rank,
+            proc.pid,
+        )
+        sock_send(
+            self._heartbeat_sender,
+            ProcessActiveRanksOutput(ranks=[global_rank], active=False),
+        )
+
+    def _poll_control(self) -> None:
+        try:
+            request = sock_recv(self._shutdown_receiver, flags=zmq.NOBLOCK)
+        except zmq.Again:
+            pass
+        else:
+            self._shutdown_dp(request)
+
+        try:
+            sock_send(self._heartbeat_sender, self.heartbeat(), flags=zmq.NOBLOCK)
+        except zmq.Again:
+            logger.debug("Dropping watchdog heartbeat because tokenizer is unavailable")
+
+    def _shutdown_dp(self, request: FaultToleranceDPCShutdownReqInput) -> None:
+        targets = set(request.target_dp_ranks)
+        for proc, dp_rank in zip(self._processes, self._process_dp_ranks):
+            if dp_rank in targets and proc.is_alive():
+                proc.kill()
+
+    def _close_sockets(self) -> None:
+        if self._heartbeat_sender is not None:
+            self._heartbeat_sender.close(linger=0)
+        if self._shutdown_receiver is not None:
+            self._shutdown_receiver.close(linger=0)

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from enum import Enum
+from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List
+
+
+class RankState(str, Enum):
+    HEALTHY = "healthy"
+    UNHEALTHY = "unhealthy"
+    DEAD = "dead"
+
+
+class FaultToleranceState:
+    def __init__(self, *, dp_size: int, strategy: str, global_rank_count: int):
+        self.dp_size = dp_size
+        self.strategy = strategy
+        self.global_rank_count = global_rank_count
+        self.global_ranks_per_dp = global_rank_count // dp_size
+        self.expected_dp_mask = [True] * dp_size
+        self.runtime_active_dp_mask = [True] * dp_size
+        self.process_alive_global_rank_mask = [True] * global_rank_count
+        self.pending_recovery_global_ranks: set[int] = set()
+        self.unhealthy_dp_ranks: set[int] = set()
+        self.ft_operation_in_progress = False
+        self.cluster_paused = False
+
+    def global_ranks_for_dp(self, dp_rank: int) -> range:
+        start = dp_rank * self.global_ranks_per_dp
+        return range(start, start + self.global_ranks_per_dp)
+
+    def global_ranks_for_dps(self, dp_ranks: Iterable[int]) -> List[int]:
+        return [
+            rank
+            for dp in sorted(set(dp_ranks))
+            for rank in self.global_ranks_for_dp(dp)
+        ]
+
+    def expand_dp_mask_to_global_rank_mask(self, dp_mask: List[bool]) -> List[bool]:
+        return [
+            dp_mask[rank // self.global_ranks_per_dp]
+            for rank in range(self.global_rank_count)
+        ]
+
+    def project_global_rank_mask_to_dp_mask(
+        self, global_rank_mask: List[bool]
+    ) -> List[bool]:
+        return [
+            all(global_rank_mask[rank] for rank in self.global_ranks_for_dp(dp))
+            for dp in range(self.dp_size)
+        ]
+
+    def process_alive_dp_mask(self) -> List[bool]:
+        return self.project_global_rank_mask_to_dp_mask(
+            self.process_alive_global_rank_mask
+        )
+
+    def expected_dp_ranks(self) -> List[int]:
+        return [rank for rank, expected in enumerate(self.expected_dp_mask) if expected]
+
+    def _rank_state(self, rank: int) -> RankState:
+        if not self.expected_dp_mask[rank] or not self.process_alive_dp_mask()[rank]:
+            return RankState.DEAD
+        if rank in self.unhealthy_dp_ranks:
+            return RankState.UNHEALTHY
+        return RankState.HEALTHY
+
+    def status_response(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "schema_version": 1,
+            "total_engines": self.dp_size,
+            "engines": [
+                {"id": rank, "status": self._rank_state(rank).value}
+                for rank in range(self.dp_size)
+            ],
+        }
+
+    def has_unresolved_expected_dp_fault(self) -> bool:
+        """Return whether an expected DP is unhealthy or has lost a process."""
+        process_alive_dp_mask = self.process_alive_dp_mask()
+        return bool(self.unhealthy_dp_ranks) or any(
+            expected and not process_alive_dp_mask[rank]
+            for rank, expected in enumerate(self.expected_dp_mask)
+        )
+
+    def is_global_admission_blocked(self, route_dp_mask: List[bool]) -> bool:
+        return (
+            not any(route_dp_mask)
+            or self.ft_operation_in_progress
+            or (self.strategy == "pause" and self.cluster_paused)
+        )
+
+    def observe_process_active_ranks(self, ranks: List[int], *, active: bool) -> None:
+        for rank in ranks:
+            self.process_alive_global_rank_mask[rank] = active
+        if not active:
+            self.pending_recovery_global_ranks.update(ranks)
+            self.cluster_paused = True
+
+    def observe_runtime_active_dp_mask(self, active_dp_mask: List[bool]) -> None:
+        self.runtime_active_dp_mask = active_dp_mask
+        self.pending_recovery_global_ranks = {
+            rank
+            for rank in self.pending_recovery_global_ranks
+            if not active_dp_mask[rank // self.global_ranks_per_dp]
+        }
+
+    def observe_rank_fault(self, rank: int) -> None:
+        if self.strategy == "pause":
+            self.unhealthy_dp_ranks.add(rank)

+        request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex

+        )

+            active_mask=active_global_rank_mask,
+        )
+        await self.send_to_scheduler(req)
+        try:

+        finally:
+            self._pending_commands.pop(request_id, None)
+
+    def _finish_shutdown_if_ready(self) -> None:
+        if self._shutdown_waiter is None:
+            return
+        targets, future = self._shutdown_waiter
+        if not future.done() and not any(
+            self.state.process_alive_global_rank_mask[rank] for rank in targets
+        ):

+
+    async def _shutdown_dp_processes(
+        self, target_dp_ranks: set[int], timeout_sec: int
+    ) -> None:
+        targets = set(self.state.global_ranks_for_dps(target_dp_ranks))
+        live_targets = {

+                ),
+            )

+        finally:
+            self._shutdown_waiter = None
+
